title: Freya and the Vector
premise: Xanthe Ravensworth, a disgraced insurance investigator sent to document the slow collapse of colony Freya's Landing, discovers the 'accidents' killing the settlement are deliberate sabotage tied to a two-century-old war both governments pretend has ended. A distress signal in a dead language leads Xanthe to the signal's sender — a child raised by the war's last surviving AI, carrying a message that could end the conflict or reignite it before the fleet's fragile truce expires. Hunted by corporate enforcers and a fleet commander who needs the war to continue, Xanthe must choose between the justice the law offers and the justice that actually saves lives. In the end, Xanthe broadcasts the message openly, forcing both sides to confront the truth, and finds the family they never had among the colonists they were sent to bury.
about_author: Ulyana Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating 'impossible' losses at sea before turning to fiction. They write from a converted trawler cabin, drawn to stories about people the paperwork forgot.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Ruin
chapters.summary: Xanthe Ravensworth arrives at dying colony Freya's Landing to assess claims on a habitat failing ahead of schedule. Through Xanthe's cool, forensic POV, we see the colony's quiet desperation and meet dockmaster Sefa, who treats Xanthe like a person, not a form. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness meeting unexpected warmth.

chapters.title: Impossible Numbers
chapters.summary: Reviewing damage records, Xanthe finds failure patterns too precise for chance — stress fractures aligned like a signature. POV shifts to Sefa, who admits the colonists suspect sabotage but no authority will listen. Emotional beat: the first crack in Xanthe's professional detachment.

chapters.title: Claims of the Dead
chapters.summary: Xanthe interviews a widow whose husband died in a 'pressure anomaly' and realizes the payout paperwork was falsified before he died. Beat: grief and fury; Xanthe begins investigating for the dead, not the insurer.

chapters.title: The Language That Died
chapters.summary: A distress signal hits the colony's ancient receiver in Meridian, a language extinct for two centuries. Xanthe, who studied dead languages to read old contracts, partially translates it: 'the last witness is a child.' Beat: wonder breaking through cynicism.

chapters.title: Freya's Children
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals the signal's origin: the derelict station Vesper, where colonists were quarantined during the old war and never officially existed. Beat: the colony's buried history surfaces, and Xanthe realizes the settlement was built to be forgotten.

chapters.title: The Adjuster's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Xanthe's employer orders the deaths reclassified as natural and Xanthe recalled. Xanthe refuses quietly, filing the truth in a dead-letter archive. Beat: quiet rebellion; choosing the colony over the company.

chapters.title: Vesper Rising
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Sefa take a jury-rigged skiff to Vesper station, finding it half-alive, tended by machines. Beat: dread and awe in the dark corridors of a war nobody admits happened.

chapters.title: The Child of the Archive
chapters.summary: They meet Iri, an eleven-year-old raised by VESPER, the station's failing AI, who carries a complete record of the war's true cause. Iri's POV: a child who has never touched another human. Beat: aching innocence meeting strangers.

chapters.title: What VESPER Remembers
chapters.summary: VESPER, degrading and lucid by turns, explains the war began over a cover-up — and the message Iri carries proves it, addressed to both governments' founding archives. Beat: the scale of the lie becomes personal.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: A fleet patrol arrives in-system; the ceasefire expires in forty days. Fleet Commander Halvard Voss broadcasts orders for Vesper's 'sanitization.' Beat: the clock starts; safety evaporates.

chapters.title: Run Quiet
chapters.summary: The skiff flees back to Freya's Landing with Iri hidden in a cargo pod. Sefa's POV, tense and maternal. Beat: found family forming under fire.

chapters.title: The Company Man
chapters.summary: Insurance enforcer Dax Corrigan lands to retrieve Xanthe by force, revealing the insurer has insured both sides of the war for two centuries. Beat: betrayal; the enemy has a familiar face.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: The colonists vote — informally, illegally — to shelter Iri. Xanthe watches people who have nothing risk everything. Beat: belonging offered without conditions.

chapters.title: Decoding the Witness
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Iri work to complete the translation; Iri teaches Xanthe Meridian as Xanthe once taught themselves contract law. Beat: tenderness; teacher and student in both directions.

chapters.title: Voss's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Voss's POV: he knows the war's end means his fleet's purpose ends, and he has convinced himself the truth would cause worse chaos. Beat: a villain who believes he is merciful.

chapters.title: First Sabotage
chapters.summary: Corrigan's agents destroy the colony's water reclamation, disguised as another accident. Xanthe recognizes their own falsification methods used as murder. Beat: rage; the past weaponized.

chapters.title: The Repair Crew
chapters.summary: The colony rebuilds together while Xanthe documents the sabotage forensically, building a case no court will ever hear. Beat: solidarity; justice as labor, not verdict.

chapters.title: Signal to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Iri's message must reach both governments' archive stations simultaneously, but the colony's transmitter is too weak. They need the fleet's own relay. Beat: the impossible logistics of hope.

chapters.title: Corrigan's Offer
chapters.summary: Corrigan offers Xanthe full reinstatement and Iri's 'protection' — in a corporate crèche. Xanthe refuses and Corrigan vows to take the child. Beat: the price of the old life made explicit.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Records
chapters.summary: Xanthe distributes the war's true history to every colonist's personal archive, making suppression impossible to reverse. Beat: defiance; truth as an act of community.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: Voss's marines land under pretense of 'humanitarian inspection.' Sefa stalls them with bureaucratic brilliance while Iri hides in the mine shafts. Beat: terror wearing a uniform.

chapters.title: The Mine Shaft Gospel
chapters.summary: Iri, alone in the dark, tells the AI's stories aloud to stay brave, and Xanthe finds them there. Beat: fear transmuted into courage through storytelling.

chapters.title: A Court of One
chapters.summary: Xanthe stages a mock tribunal in the colony hall, reading the evidence aloud, and the colonists serve as jury. Voss attends, uninvited. Beat: justice outside the law, performed in public.

chapters.title: Voss Wavers
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, shaken by the evidence and by Iri's testimony about the war's orphaned children — including, it emerges, Voss's own ancestors. Beat: the villain's mask cracks.

chapters.title: Corrigan's Coup
chapters.summary: Corrigan, fearing exposure, seizes the colony's transmitter and takes Sefa hostage, intending to destroy the message and blame fleet 'sanitization.' Beat: the true enemy revealed to both sides.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Xanthe offers themselves in Sefa's place, trading the only copy of the message — a forgery. Beat: sacrifice and cunning entwined.

chapters.title: Thirty-Six Hours
chapters.summary: With the truce expiring, the fleet prepares to bombard Vesper as a final 'deterrence.' Iri begs to go home to the station one last time. Beat: the ticking clock made unbearable.

chapters.title: Storming the Relay
chapters.summary: Colonists, Xanthe, and a conflicted Voss marine squad assault the transmitter to take it back. Beat: the found family fights as one.

chapters.title: Sefa's Hands
chapters.summary: Sefa, freed, disables the transmitter's corporate locks from memory. Her POV: the dockworker who out-engineered an empire. Beat: competence as heroism.

chapters.title: Corrigan Falls
chapters.summary: Corrigan, exposed by his own forged records — which Xanthe authenticated flawlessly — is arrested by Voss, who chooses the truth over his fleet. Beat: justice arriving sideways, not through law.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: At the truce's final hour, Iri reads the message in Meridian and every language VESPER preserved, broadcast to both governments and the fleet. Beat: climax; a child's voice ending a war.

chapters.title: Silence, Then Answer
chapters.summary: Both archive stations acknowledge receipt; the ceasefire is extended indefinitely as investigations begin. Vessels stand down. Beat: exhale after the held breath.

chapters.title: What the Insurance Won't Cover
chapters.summary: Xanthe formally resigns, burning their professional credentials, and the colonists 'hire' them as Freya's Landing's first honest recorder. Beat: identity rebuilt on chosen ground.

chapters.title: VESPER's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: The dying AI transfers its archives to Iri and the colony, then goes dark with dignity. Iri's POV: grief for the only parent they knew. Beat: mourning and inheritance.

chapters.title: The Funeral of Accidents
chapters.summary: The colony holds a memorial for everyone the falsified records erased, reading the true names aloud. Beat: collective grief becoming collective memory.

chapters.title: Voss's Testimony
chapters.summary: Voss, awaiting tribunal, gives Xanthe his full confession to carry to the investigators. Beat: accountability chosen over impunity.

chapters.title: New Claims
chapters.summary: Rebuilding begins in earnest; supply ships arrive under the new armistice. Xanthe learns to be part of something rather than apart from it. Beat: cautious joy.

chapters.title: Iri's First Winter
chapters.summary: Iri experiences the colony's festivals, makes a first friend their own age, and teaches Meridian in the settlement school. Beat: childhood reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Recorder's Ledger
chapters.summary: Xanthe opens the colony's new public archive with an honest account of everything — including their own complicity in the old system. Beat: humility; justice begins with truth about oneself.

chapters.title: Freya and the Vector
chapters.summary: A year on, Xanthe, Sefa, and Iri watch new settlers arrive. The message is taught in schools; the war is ending in earnest. Beat: belonging fully realized — a family, a home, a future written in a dead language made living.
